BODATA\\KI\\KISCENER\\KI11\\PRIKIC01.MOV: This is the ear Peter cut off the soldier in Gethsemane, the night Jesus was arrested.

While the soldier was carried into his house and a doctor was called, his wife secretly picked up the ear and kept it in a small box.
Here the ear lay, still bleeding, untouched by the passing years.
Now, long after the soldier and his wife have turned to dust, the ear still bleeds.

BODATA\\KI\\KISCENER\\KI11\\PRIKIC04.MOV: These are the tears the Virgin Mary wept at the cross, kept by her maid in this little bottle.

BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE11.MOV: I remember a blackbird singing early one morning. The grass was wet.
I was in a huge meadow full of dandelions. It seemed to go on forever.
The only thing blocking the view was a few bushes.
From behind them a dog came running towards me, tail wagging, a stick in its mouth.
It stopped beside me and dropped the stick, put its paws down eagerly and started barking.
It looked like it was laughing. We ran and played all morning.
It was the first day it came home with me, and I knew I'd never be alone again.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE12.MOV: I remember once when Dad and I were out walking. We were on our way to a meeting at school.
It was a warm day, and we walked past the sweet shop.
The one with the red sign outside. I hardly ever got any sweets.
But that day he stopped and went in.
I stood outside and watched him through the window.
He bought a big, big bag of pick-and-mix, and when he came out he gave it to me.
He smiled, but in a strange, strained way that put me on my guard.
I hurried to stuff some sweets in my mouth in case he changed his mind, but he didn't.
Instead he started talking about the meeting and promised me a puppy if I behaved.
I knew I'd never get one, but I liked the idea.
I liked it when he talked like that, because then he felt like a normal dad, like on TV.
He talked almost the whole way.
Said I mustn't say anything bad about him, because he was my dad.
And if I did, some nasty men would turn up and take me to a children's home.
And in children's homes they beat you.
And you have to sleep with the light off.
And you have to stay there forever.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE13.MOV: I remember sitting in a sunny garden with the boy next door.
We sat at a little garden table with white chairs.
On the table was a small typewriter he'd been given for his birthday.
I think I was seven, and he asked if we should tell each other secrets.
He was my best friend, I said.
So I told him about the time Dad killed my dog with a hammer.
It was the first time I'd told anyone about Dad's dark side.
The boy next door went completely quiet.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE14.MOV: It was at the neighbours'. They had a really cosy living room.
Everything was more worn than at our place, but in a nice, safe way.
I sat on the sofa, covered in blankets.
The fire crackled in the fireplace and the whole room smelled good.
We watched some old film. I think it was Laurel and Hardy.
There were biscuits and sweets on the table, and next to me sat my best friend, the boy next door.
I think we were seven. Anyway, he had short hair and new front teeth, just like me.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDEBI1.MOV: The flames flickered in the draught. It was autumn, and the wind crept in under the door.
A lonely little leaf had found its way in when I came.
It lay spinning in the draught on the floor.
It was cold in the church, but it still felt safe.
The priest sat beside me on the steps up to the altar.
He'd turned off the lights and was about to lock up when I came.
Through the window we watched the wind tear at the bare branches and the clouds hang up there.
Now hidden, now revealed by the passing clouds.
The priest sat watching me for a long time without saying anything.
Then he said: I think you're right.
Your soul is no longer whole, but I don't think you can kill them.
He was talking about my mother and father.
He was the only one I'd ever told.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDEBI2.MOV: One afternoon I sat in the priest's little room with the old desk.
Outside stood some tiny, newly planted trees.
They were so beautiful that I felt cold and hard by comparison.
I think I remember that afternoon so well because I told him more details than before.
I remember he sat there, pale,
elbows propped on the desk, and asked if there really was nothing he could do.
And I told him it would only make things worse.
That I'd turn eighteen in three years, and my backside was tougher than Dad's belt.

Maybe I'm doing something wrong, the child thinks.
A seed of thought that leads to sickness.

They want something from you, or you want to give them something.
It's fading. I have to sleep.

BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE21.MOV: I remember our shed. It was always neatly tidied.
At one end were Dad's tools and the workbench.
The birch rod lay on the workbench.
I always had to go and fetch it myself.
And every time it felt like it was lying there waiting for me.
Going up the stairs with the rod, I always held it far away from me.
I deserve it. I deserve it. I deserve it.
And I told myself he did it because he loved me.
Though I knew I was lying.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE22.MOV: I'd just woken up that morning.
Dad dragged me out of bed.
I remember his face was twisted with rage.
He said he'd teach me what happens to boys who don't stop wetting the bed.
I thought he was going to hit me, but he dragged me into the living room.
It took a while before I understood what he meant to do.
He pulled me over to the tiled stove and opened it with a rag in his hand.
It was as if the whole room would explode.
Inside the stove I watched blisters rise on my hand.
Something in the stove had taken over, made me invulnerable.
It had been born from the fire of the pain.
And it became part of me.
As if it was no longer my hand burning.
As if I was standing outside myself.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE23.MOV: The room was full of light and smelled clean.
The walls were white, and everything in the room was neutral and calm in a reassuring way.
There were no secrets there.
Everything was what it seemed.
The little room was next to the craft room.
There were glass cabinets full of clay objects waiting to be fired in the kiln.
I sat at a table with a perfectly smooth top.
I think I was about seven.
In front of me I had paint and paper, and my painting was taking shape.
Everything worked and felt so easy.
Over by the wall stood a woman.
She had her hair up, a white blouse and a mid-length skirt.
She was my teacher.
A while later there was a knock at the door, and a man with a beard and glasses came in.
He stood beside my teacher and looked at my drawing.
It felt good.
Something spun inside me and my face went all warm.
But I pretended nothing was wrong.
Then my teacher showed him some of my other drawings.
I could see he was impressed.
Both of them praised me.
I don't remember what they said, or what they wanted the drawings for.
On the way home I hummed a tune I'd made up myself.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE24.MOV: It was at school, one of the last lessons.
I felt tired and uneasy, because I knew I'd soon be going home.
The teacher stood at the front by her desk.
She was a prim little lady, skirt and hair up.
She put up four pictures on the board.
At the bottom of the pictures the words were written.
I thought there was something nasty about the pictures.
They said ice, eel, and mummy and daddy.
She asked me to read the words out, and the pictures of the mummy and daddy changed.
They turned hard and cold as ice, their eyes vanished and their mouths gaped open.
The eel started to move and crawled into their mouths.
I felt sick and was about to throw up.
Suddenly it was as if everything vanished, and the pictures were all that existed.
I was standing in the middle of the schoolyard again.
My teacher came walking towards me.
I realised that I liked her.
Still, I didn't let her touch me when she carefully reached out her hand.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE25.MOV: I remember the dark. I was lying in bed in my room.
The light was off, and out in the dark I could see shadows moving.
They turned into misty, shadowy creatures that seemed to be trying to grab me.
They had long, sharp nails like scalpels that scraped the floor and the bed as they crept closer and closer.
And one of them licked its lips with a forked tongue.
They came so close to the bed that I could hear their heavy panting.
Then suddenly he was there, in the dark.
He had fire in his eyes, glowing red.
He came in through my window and took care of me.
And with one finger he drew a circle around me.
And nothing could get inside that circle.
None of the things crawling in the dark could reach me.
It was like a glass dome had settled between me and the world.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE26.MOV: I was up in my room.
All my toy soldiers lay scattered across the floor like little ants.
It was a warm late-summer day and the window was open.
And the air outside was thick, like just before a storm.
I remember I stopped playing when I heard the shouting out on the stairs.
When I went over to the window I felt a warm gust of wind from outside.
A wind that whispered in the trees and bushes.
It felt as if I rose from the floor and flew out into the open.
It was as if the whole world had suddenly stopped.
And when I turned my head to look around,
I could see my empty body sitting on the floor, playing among the soldiers.
Behind me the door opened, and my father came in with his belt in his hand.
I floated outside the window and watched.
But in some strange way I didn't care.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE27.MOV: I came home from school as usual.
It was a real autumn day, and I can still remember the smell of my wet clothes.
I took off my jacket and carried it to the living room to hang it up to dry.
We had one of those big, clunky radiators they had back then.
When I came into the room I saw my father sitting completely still on the sofa.
His face was like stone, leaning forward so he was glaring at me.
I didn't understand what was wrong.
Then I saw the hammer beside him on the sofa.
I ran up to my room, and there lay my dog.
I held it in my lap until it stopped.
I didn't cry. I didn't get angry either.
I just became like a stain on the wallpaper.
Nobody came into the room until dinnertime.
Dad told me to wash my hands before I came to the table.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE28.MOV: I was sitting in the living room that afternoon.
It had been grey and gloomy outside.
But suddenly the clouds broke.
And light came pouring in through the window.
Then it was as if I was in the living room for the first time.
The chairs, the lamps, and the worn sofa where my parents sat.
Everything was clean and tidy.
But it was as if the sunlight exposed all the cracks beneath the surface.
Not just in the furniture, but under my parents' skin too.
All the ugliness broke through.
First as black spots.
Then as peeling strips of skin.
And the flesh underneath was laid bare.
And suddenly I noticed I was in several parts of the room at once.
Fear huddled in one corner of the room.
Another part knelt before my father, wagging its tail.
The fire smashed a window without anyone hearing or reacting.
That day I saw the vileness, and something inside me was embraced.
Not by the pain, not by the hate, and not by the wish to be loved.
But by a longing to touch something purer than that.
Something that was in the light.
Something that was invulnerable.
BODATA\\MINDER\\MINDE29.MOV: I stood at the end of the church's long aisle with Dad's sinewy hand in mine.
It was quite dark in the church, but there were people in the pews.
They were dressed in their best, and all stared at me as I walked up the aisle.
From the cross above, Jesus stared down at me with bloody hands and a crown of thorns.
I looked at him as I walked up to the little coffin where my brother lay.
Everyone talked about the terrible accident.
But I knew it hadn't been an accident.
My father looked as if someone had suddenly shaken him awake.
A shadow of fear passed over his face.
